messages:
jeff_oncall: Incident alert — tokenizer pods on prod-east are repeatedly OOM-killing (CPU saturation). Started seeing 5xx spikes at 13:02 UTC. Incident-bot triggered page.

incident-bot: [ALERT] high_cpu_usage: /service/tokenizer (pod/tokenizer-7f9d6) CPU > 98% for > 2m. Escalated to #incidents and on-call.

jeff_oncall: Quick diagnostics: kubectl top pod shows tokenizer at 99% cpu, host node cpu at 93%. Pod logs show repeated Python "Killed" with no stacktrace — classic SIGKILL from OOM. Also saw intermittent CUDA errors in runtime logs when GPU-backed variant gets scheduled: "CUDA error: out of memory" followed by container restart.

madi_eng: Adding context — we shipped tokenizer v3.1.2 rollout last night that changed batch pre-processing and added per-request regex passes. Hypothesis: pathological prompts trigger quadratic token processing, blowing CPU and memory on the pre-tokenization step.

ryan_sre: Running live: `kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=tokenizer -o wide` and `kubectl top node prod-east-3` — will post outputs.

ryan_sre: (paste) pods: tokenizer-7f9d6 Running 1/1 2Gi, node=prod-east-3. Node CPU 92%.

madi_eng: Logs snippet: ```
2026-03-15T12:59:31Z tokenizer INFO processing prompt id=abc123 size=1.2e6 chars
2026-03-15T12:59:31Z tokenizer WARN regex pass 1 iterations=120000
2026-03-15T12:59:32Z tokenizer ERROR MemoryError
2026-03-15T12:59:32Z kernel: [pid 10234] Out of memory: Killed process 10234 (python) total-vm:2048000kB
```

jeff_oncall: Customer impact — we're seeing ~12% of generation requests returning 500/503 in prod-east region, tail latency >20s. Notifying SRE/CS. AcmeHealth on Dedicated reported degraded throughput on their /generate route.

ops_intake: tagging customers: AcmeHealth, BrightRetail. CS notified via #customer-impact and sending status to affected accounts.

jeff_oncall: Immediate mitigations we should attempt now (in order):
1) Scale tokenizer replicas down to 0 for GPU variant and scale CPU-safe variant to handle baseline (avoid CUDA OOM).
2) Rollback tokenizer to v3.0.9 (pre-regex-change) to stop pathological processing.
3) Temporarily apply an admission webhook or mutating config to limit max_prompt_length to 200k chars to mitigate bad prompts.
4) If needed, cordon and drain the hottest node, then restart nodes to clear kernel OOM state.

madi_eng: I'm preparing a rollback to v3.0.9 now. Also pushing a hotfix to short-circuit the expensive regex for huge inputs (`if len(prompt) > 200k: return reject`), will push as config flag.

ryan_sre: Executing step 1: `kubectl scale deployment/tokenizer-gpu --replicas=0 -n prod` -> DONE. `kubectl scale deployment/tokenizer-cpu --replicas=6 -n prod` -> scaled to 6, monitoring. CPU usage dropping slightly.

tess_support: CS update sent: "We're investigating high latency and errors in the east region. A mitigation is in progress; some requests may be delayed up to 30 minutes. We're prioritizing dedicated customers."

madi_eng: Rolling back: `kubectl set image deployment/tokenizer-cpu tokenizer=redwood/tokenizer:v3.0.9` -> rollout started. Also toggled feature flag `ENABLE_HEAVY_REGEX=false` in configmap `tokenizer-config`.

incident-bot: Deployment rollout event: tokenizer-cpu updated (rc=3/3).

ryan_sre: Post-rollback metrics (10m): 500s dropped from 12% -> 3%, CPU usage on tokenizer pods from 98% -> 55% on average. One node still showing kernel oom events — will drain it.

jeff_oncall: Good. Next actions: drain prod-east-3 to clear kernel oom/shallow swap state. `kubectl drain prod-east-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. Also patch kubelet `evictionHard` to avoid immediate pod kills if node pressure transient? Let's not touch kubelet live unless necessary.

ryan_sre: Draining node now, pods rescheduled. Node had repeated oom_killer logs for python processes across multiple containers; likely the big prompt processing overloaded node-level memory. Rebooting node after drain.

madi_eng: Added temporary request-level guard in front of tokenizer: we now enforce max_prompt_tokens=50000 at nginx layer for prod-east (config pushed). Prompts exceeding that return 400 with helpful error message.

jeff_oncall: Customer impact assessment update: AcmeHealth had 18 requests affected over last hour, no data loss, only request failures and retries. Recommend follow-up email explaining mitigation and the prompt size guard.

tess_support: I'll draft the AcmeHealth note and coordinate CS response.

madi_eng: Root cause hypothesis: v3.1.2 introduced an unbounded regex pass over input to normalize whitespace/emoji sequences. For pathological inputs (e.g., generated by bad client concatenation), the pass becomes O(n^2) and exhausts process memory/CPU. Also observed some GPU-scheduled pods still attempted allocation and hit CUDA OOM before crash — we disabled GPU variant earlier. Fix path: revert to v3.0.9, add input size checks, rewrite regex to linear pass, add unit tests and a fuzz test for huge inputs.

jeff_oncall: Severity — S2 incident (partial region degradation, dedicated customer impact). Declaring incident resolved once we confirm metrics stable for 30 minutes and follow-up PR merged with safeguards.

ryan_sre: Monitoring shows stable for 18 minutes. Node reboot succeeded; no further kernel oom logs.

madi_eng: Opened PR #5487: "tokenizer: enforce prompt length and linearize regex" with tests and rollout plan to v3.1.3-canary.

jeff_oncall: Handoff to madi — I'm going offline in 10m. Madi, you'll be primary for follow-ups and postmortem. Make sure to include timeline, RCA, customer impact numbers, and remediation.

madi_eng: Acknowledged. I'll own postmortem and follow-ups. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

jeff_oncall: Closing remarks: good quick ops work — scaling and rollback stopped immediate pain. Next steps: postmortem, deploy better input guards in the tokenizer and edge, add quota/size limits in SDKs, and consider a safety net in the autoscaler to avoid scheduling heavy tokenizers on low-memory nodes.

incident-bot: Incident state changed: acknowledged -> mitigated by oncall @jeff_oncall.

madi_eng: Final note: follow-up ticket created INF-223: "Prevent tokenizer prompt-processing spike -> CPU OOM" with action items: regex rewrite, canary rollout, SDK validation, stronger telemetry for pre-tokenization latency.

ryan_sre: Last check: 200s/500s back to baseline, no remaining oom_killer messages in node logs. Marking as monitored."
